what: Anywhere on screen, moving the mouse makes each layer trail behind by ‹distance from screen center to cursor × strength› over 1.2s power3, which creates depth between layers — the front photo with strength .09 moves a lot, the back photo with .035 moves a little

options.depth: Strength when a layer has no data-depth, default .05
options.lerp: If set, instead of a tween each frame catches up to the cursor by this fraction and places the layer immediately (source site .06). A negative strength pushes away from the cursor.
options.axis: x · y · xy (default) — axis to follow
options.data-clamp: When put on a layer element, limits that layer’s movement to ±px (Brand background art 40)
options.rest-x: In lerp, x (px) before the cursor first moves, default screen center — Brand 0
options.rest-y: y (px) in lerp before the cursor first moves, default is the screen center

note: Since GSAP uses the layer’s transform, put translate for things like centering inside the layer or on an outer element. Not attached on touch devices (no hover). While the panel is offscreen it does not follow the mouse (once it enters, it follows from the next movement).

from.where: From the original site’s root section code (quickTo x·y 1.2s power3, strength .09·.06·.035, window mousemove) — when measured at 1440 the original did not actually move, so it is not attached to the site copy and is kept only as a part

index.html .kv — original hero: the cursor x is chased by .06 each frame, and (screen center − chased x) × .035 (±40px), .02, .015 pushes the picture plate, the upper roots and the dove (horizontal only)
from.options: lerp: .06; axis: x; rest-x: 0 · layers data-depth -.035 (data-clamp 40)·-.02·-.015

from.where: index.html .ky-stage five pencil drawing layers — the original uses parallax-js 3.1.0 defaults (scalar 10 · friction .1 · opposite direction) with data-depth .24·.1·.12·.06·0, and the copy also uses parallax-js as is
from.options: lerp: .1 · layer data-depth set negative (opposite to the cursor) — strength = depth × panel width × .1 ÷ half screen width
